items.example: Toute la famille était là.
items.example_en: The whole family was there.
items.note: The double l sounds like a y.

items.example: Mes parents habitent à la campagne.
items.example_en: My parents live in the countryside.
items.note: Also means relatives in general: un parent éloigné, a distant relative.

items.example: Mon frère est plus jeune que moi.
items.example_en: My brother is younger than me.
items.note: la soeur is sister.

items.example: Leur fils a commencé l'école.
items.example_en: Their son has started school.
items.note: The l is silent and the s sounds: /fis/, not /fil/.

items.example: Sa fille a huit ans.
items.example_en: His daughter is eight.
items.note: Means both daughter and girl; ma fille is only daughter.

items.example: On va chez mes grands-parents dimanche.
items.example_en: We're going to my grandparents' on Sunday.
items.note: chez plus a person means at their place.

items.example: Mon mari cuisine mieux que moi.
items.example_en: My husband cooks better than I do.
items.note: ma femme is my wife, and also means woman.

items.example: Je sors avec mon copain ce soir.
items.example_en: I'm going out with my boyfriend tonight.
items.note: With mon/ma it means partner; with un it just means a friend.

items.example: Il est célibataire depuis un an.
items.example_en: He's been single for a year.
items.note: Same form for men and women.

items.example: Ils sont mariés depuis dix ans.
items.example_en: They've been married for ten years.
items.note: Agrees: mariée, mariés, mariées.

items.example: C'est un ami proche de la famille.
items.example_en: He's a close friend of the family.

items.example: Je m'entends bien avec ma soeur.
items.example_en: I get along well with my sister.
items.note: Literally to hear each other well.

items.example: Elle est grande et mince.
items.example_en: She is tall and slim.
items.note: Before the noun it means great: un grand homme, a great man.

items.example: Il a les cheveux bruns et courts.
items.example_en: He has short brown hair.
items.note: French says he HAS the hair, with the definite article.

items.example: Elle a les yeux verts comme sa mère.
items.example_en: She has green eyes like her mother.
items.note: Singular is un oeil, an irregular pair worth memorising.

items.example: Mon collègue porte des lunettes rondes.
items.example_en: My colleague wears round glasses.
items.note: porter covers both wearing and carrying.

items.example: Tu as l'air fatigué.
items.example_en: You look tired.
items.note: Followed directly by an adjective, no comme.

items.example: Elle ressemble beaucoup à son père.
items.example_en: She looks a lot like her father.
items.note: Always with à, never a direct object.

items.example: Le voisin est très gentil avec nous.
items.example_en: The neighbour is very kind to us.
items.note: Feminine gentille, with the l sounded.

items.example: Ton frère est vraiment drôle.
items.example_en: Your brother is really funny.
items.note: Before the noun it means odd: une drôle d'histoire.

items.example: C'est une équipe travailleuse.
items.example_en: It's a hard-working team.
items.note: Feminine travailleuse.

items.example: Il est têtu comme une mule.
items.example_en: He's as stubborn as a mule.

items.example: Elle est de bonne humeur aujourd'hui.
items.example_en: She's in a good mood today.
items.note: Opposite: de mauvaise humeur.

items.example: Malgré tout, elle a bon caractère.
items.example_en: In spite of everything, she's even-tempered.
items.note: caractère is temperament, not a person in a story (that is un personnage).

items.example: Je suis content de te voir.
items.example_en: I'm happy to see you.
items.note: Everyday word for happy; heureux is deeper.

items.example: La fin du film est triste.
items.example_en: The end of the film is sad.
items.note: Same form for both genders.

items.example: Je suis fatigué, je vais me coucher.
items.example_en: I'm tired, I'm going to bed.

items.example: J'ai peur de prendre l'avion.
items.example_en: I'm afraid of flying.
items.note: French HAS fear. Same pattern: avoir faim, soif, froid, chaud, raison.

items.example: J'en ai marre de ce bruit.
items.example_en: I'm fed up with this noise.
items.note: Very common in speech, informal but not rude.

items.example: Les réunions le matin, ça me stresse.
items.example_en: Morning meetings stress me out.
items.note: The pronoun me lands before the verb, as always.

items.example: Tu as gagné ? Ça alors !
items.example_en: You won? Well I never!
items.note: Mild, friendly surprise.

items.example: Il a démissionné ? C'est pas vrai !
items.example_en: He quit? No way!
items.note: Spoken French drops the ne: c'est pas rather than ce n'est pas.

items.example: Il ne pleut plus ? Tant mieux.
items.example_en: It stopped raining? So much the better.
items.note: Opposite: tant pis, too bad.

items.example: Tu viens ? Ça dépend de l'heure.
items.example_en: Are you coming? It depends on the time.
items.note: dépendre always takes de.

items.example: Moi ça va, et toi ?
items.example_en: I'm fine, and you?
items.note: The cheapest way to keep a conversation going.

items.example: Bref, on s'est bien amusés.
items.example_en: Anyway, we had a good time.
items.note: Wraps up a rambling story. Extremely common in speech.
